annotationRationale: Writing the decimal pattern as powers of ten exposes the alternating powers of 100 modulo 101, which determine all successful exponents.
sourceMethod: Followed the official even/odd exponent split using 100 ≡ -1 modulo 101. The odd-exponent calculation is clarified as residues 11 and -9, equivalently 11 and 92, correcting the source's stated 9.

review.mathCheck: The exponent range is correctly 2 through 2019. Since 100 has remainder −1 modulo 101, even exponents work exactly when n≡2 modulo 4; odd exponents give residues 11 or −9 and never work. The inclusive count from 2 through 2018 is 505, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 13's parity split and alternating powers of 100. It correctly repairs the printed source's sign slip: the odd-exponent residues are −9 and 11.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed modular-power skill and supporting algebraic encoding match the method. Both parity cases and the inclusive endpoint count are explained.
